extract_protocol_ch1: Blood was collected in EDTA tubes within a 90 min window for all participants of the study. Pools were resuspended in Cell Staining Buffer (Biolegend) and incubated with Fc Receptor Blocking Solution (Biolegend) at 20mg/mL for 10 minutes on ice. Cells were then stained with a cocktail of 140 TotalSeq-C oligo-tagged antibodies (Biolegend) for 30 minutes at 4°C. Stained cells were washed in PBS containing 1% BSA, filtered through a 70uM filter, and re-suspended in a final solution of PBS containing 0.04% BSA.

Stained cells (n=60,000) were loaded on the Chromium Controller (10X Genomics) for GEM generation. The cDNA libraries were generated using the Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 5’ v1.1 Library Kit for gene expression (GEX) and the Chromium Single Cell 5’ Feature Barcode Library kit for antibody derived tag (ADT) according to manufacturer’s instructions (10X Genomics). Each batch of 14-16 samples was sampled four times to prepare four independent cDNA libraries per batch to obtain a sufficient number of cells per sample. Raw feature-barcode matrices were imported and analyzed using Seurat (v4.0.3).

Each library was demultiplexed to map individual cells to their sample of origin using freemuxlet (vAug2021), SNP profiles were mapped to the genotypes of individual participants from bulk RNA-seq using bcftools gtcheck (v1.10.2), and inter-sample doublets and empty droplets were removed.
DoubletFinder (v2.0.3) was used to filter barcodes containing heterotypic intra-sample doublets.

After generating single-cell count data from sequencing reads and performing quality control, the identification of cell subsets in the follow-up data was performed using Azimuth. The Seurat object from original baseline data was converted to Azimuth reference, and the follow-up dataset was mapped onto it using Azimuth, which provided predicted cell subset labels for single cells.

Feature-barcode matrices were obtained for each library by aligning the raw fastqs of gene expression to GRCh38 reference genome (Gencode v32-primary assembly) and the raw fastqs of surface protein expression to a TotalSeq-C antibody reference panel using the Cell Ranger count. Raw feature-barcode matrices were imported and analyzed using Seurat (v4.0.3).

Each library was demultiplexed to map individual cells to their sample of origin using freemuxlet (vAug2021), SNP profiles were mapped to the genotypes of individual participants from bulk RNA-seq using bcftools gtcheck (v1.10.2), and inter-sample doublets and empty droplets were removed.
DoubletFinder (v2.0.3) was used to filter barcodes containing heterotypic intra-sample doublets.

Barcodes containing less than 100 genes and genes that are detected in fewer than 3 cells were removed. We further filtered out the barcodes based on library-specific cutoffs for the number of genes per cell (nFeature_RNA <300-800 and >6,000), the number of unique molecular indexes (UMIs) per cell (nCount_RNA <400-2,000 and >40,000), mitochondrial content (>15%), and ribosomal content (<8-15% and >60%) to remove poor quality cells. The RNA and ADT count data for the resulting high-quality cell-barcodes are provided here.

For processing of follow-up timepoint, the baseline samples were reanalyzed along with the the follow-up timepoint (separated by ~19 months). After generating single-cell count data from sequencing reads and performing quality control, the identification of cell subsets in the follow-up data was performed using Azimuth. The Seurat object from original baseline data was converted to Azimuth reference, and the follow-up dataset was mapped onto it using Azimuth, which provided predicted cell subset labels for single cells.

Each batch of 14-16 samples was sampled four times to prepare four independent cDNA libraries per batch to obtain a sufficient number of cells per sample. The libraries were subsequently sequenced on a NovaSeq 6000 S4 platform (Illumina).

extract_protocol_ch1: Blood was collected in EDTA tubes within a 90 min window for all participants of the study. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) were obtained by density gradient centrifugation of whole blood at 800g for 30 min at room temperature without brake, using Ficoll-Paque (Cytiva). Isolated cells were cryopreserved in a solution containing fetal Bovine Serum and 10% DMSO (Sigma). Thawed PBMC suspensions from 14-16 individuals were pooled together with equivalent numbers to a total of 1 million live cells. Pools were resuspended in Cell Staining Buffer (Biolegend) and incubated with Fc Receptor Blocking Solution (Biolegend) at 20mg/mL for 10 minutes on ice. Cells were then stained with a cocktail of 140 TotalSeq-C oligo-tagged antibodies (Biolegend) for 30 minutes at 4°C. Stained cells were washed in PBS containing 1% BSA, filtered through a 70uM filter, and re-suspended in a final solution of PBS containing 0.04% BSA.

Stained cells (n=60,000) were loaded on the Chromium Controller (10X Genomics) for GEM generation. The cDNA libraries were generated using the Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 5’ v1.1 Library Kit for gene expression (GEX) and the Chromium Single Cell 5’ Feature Barcode Library kit for antibody derived tag (ADT) according to manufacturer’s instructions (10X Genomics). Each batch of 14-16 samples was sampled four times to prepare four independent cDNA libraries per batch to obtain a sufficient number of cells per sample. The libraries were subsequently sequenced on a NovaSeq 6000 S4 platform (Illumina).
data_processing: Sequencer-obtained bcl files were demultiplexed using mkfastq program from Cell Ranger v6.0.2 (10x Genomics). Feature-barcode matrices were obtained for each library by aligning the raw fastqs of gene expression to GRCh38 reference genome (Gencode v32-primary assembly) and the raw fastqs of surface protein expression to a TotalSeq-C antibody reference panel using the Cell Ranger count. Raw feature-barcode matrices were imported and analyzed using Seurat (v4.0.3).

Each library was demultiplexed to map individual cells to their sample of origin using freemuxlet (vAug2021), SNP profiles were mapped to the genotypes of individual participants from bulk RNA-seq using bcftools gtcheck (v1.10.2), and inter-sample doublets and empty droplets were removed.
DoubletFinder (v2.0.3) was used to filter barcodes containing heterotypic intra-sample doublets.

Barcodes containing less than 100 genes and genes that are detected in fewer than 3 cells were removed. We further filtered out the barcodes based on library-specific cutoffs for the number of genes per cell (nFeature_RNA <300-800 and >6,000), the number of unique molecular indexes (UMIs) per cell (nCount_RNA <400-2,000 and >40,000), mitochondrial content (>15%), and ribosomal content (<8-15% and >60%) to remove poor quality cells. The RNA and ADT count data for the resulting high-quality cell-barcodes are provided here.

For processing of follow-up timepoint, the baseline samples were reanalyzed along with the the follow-up timepoint (separated by ~19 months). After generating single-cell count data from sequencing reads and performing quality control, the identification of cell subsets in the follow-up data was performed using Azimuth. The Seurat object from original baseline data was converted to Azimuth reference, and the follow-up dataset was mapped onto it using Azimuth, which provided predicted cell subset labels for single cells.
